subject: Criteria weighting + rollback triggers for evaluation (MAP)
messages:

Subject: Proposed MAP and acceptance checkpoints

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the model latency and hallucination controls looked promising. Tom and I sketched a short mutual action plan to move toward a pilot and eventual production signoff. Attached is our draft MAP (MAP-ClarityHealth-v1.xlsx).

High level asks from our side:
- Clear pass/fail for the evaluation so procurement can sign off (we need a binary go/no-go).
- A short list of acceptance tests we can run in our environment (3–5 tests).
- A rollback/stop condition in case accuracy or data leakage concerns surface.

Can you propose a simple decision heuristic (weighted criteria or threshold) we can use to make the final call? Our legal and procurement teams are on a tight December cadence — if we can run a 1-week canary the week of Dec 6, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Bethany Clark
Senior Product Manager — AI
ClarityHealth

Subject: Re: Proposed MAP and acceptance checkpoints

Hi Bethany —

Appreciate the clarity. I reviewed your MAP and added a lightweight rubric that maps to pass/fail outcomes. See attached (redwood-eval-rubric-v1.pdf). Quick summary of our proposal:

- Weighted criteria (total 100 points):
  - Reliability / uptime & error rate (25)
  - Latency (p95) and throughput under typical load (20)
  - Accuracy / hallucination tolerance on target prompts (30)
  - Data controls / auditability (15)
  - Integration complexity / manifest issues (10)

- Decision heuristic: succeed if weighted score >= 75 OR if all three of the following critical gates are met:
  1) p95 latency <= 220ms in your VPC test,
  2) hallucination rate <= 6% on the evaluation prompt set,
  3) no PII leakage events in replayed logs.

- Canary plan: 1 week with production-like traffic (we suggest Dec 6–12). If the canary fails a critical gate, we trigger an immediate rollback and a post-mortem.

Can Marissa & Karthik weigh in on concrete acceptance tests and the exact rollback thresholds? If everyone agrees, we'll update the MAP spreadsheet and share a final signoff template.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-eval-rubric-v1.pdf (PDF stub, 4 pages)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bethany Clark <beth@clarityhealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@clarityhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: acceptance tests, weighting clarifications, and rollback triggers

Evelyn / Karthik — pulling together concrete, testable acceptance items so Beth's procurement team has what they need. Draft below; I've also attached a plaintext tests file for engineers (acceptance-tests.md).

Acceptance tests (run against replayed production traffic where possible):
1) Latency test (performance): 95th percentile response time <= 220ms for the trimmed prompt set at 100 rps sustained for 10 minutes. Failure mode: p95 > 300ms or sustained errors > 2% -> auto-fail.

2) Cost/throughput sanity check (economics): Average token cost per successful response within 15% of forecast. Failure mode: cost > forecast by 30%+ for 2 consecutive measurement windows -> flag for pause and review.

3) Hallucination / factuality (quality): On a curated set of 200 prompts, model produces incorrect or fabricated assertions in <= 6% of cases (manual review sampling + automated checks). Failure mode: > 10% incorrect -> immediate rollback.

4) Data control / exfiltration (security): No PII or sensitive string matches in generated outputs for the replayed set. Any confirmed match -> immediate stop and incident review.

5) Integrations (stability): All API routes must return expected schema and error codes. Breaking schema changes -> fail.

Decision heuristics (scoring):
- Map the 5 tests to weights per Evelyn's rubric (25/20/30/15/10). Compute a weighted score (0–100). Pass if weighted score >= 75.
- Critical gates (must not fail): Data control and Hallucination tests are designated critical. If either critical gate hits the "immediate rollback" condition, the canary ends with an automatic failure regardless of weighted score.

Rollback and mitigation triggers:
- Soft-fail: Any non-critical threshold breach -> pause canary, collect logs, 4-hour remediation window.
- Hard-fail: Critical gate or repeat high-severity errors -> immediate rollback to previous model version and freeze MAP signoff until remediation is approved by both parties.

Operational notes:
- We'll run automated checks hourly and send a digest to both teams.
- Post-canar y report template: 1) pass/fail, 2) weighted score, 3) raw metrics, 4) incidents and R/A/C/E.

Attachment: acceptance-tests.md (plaintext, contains test commands and expected outputs)

Thoughts? If we lock these thresholds, I can update the MAP spreadsheet and provide a signoff template for procurement.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Criteria weighting + rollback triggers for evaluation (MAP)

All — this looks good and actionable. Confirming ClarityHealth's acceptance of the following:

- Run the 1-week canary Dec 6–12 (production-like traffic).
- We will evaluate using the weighted rubric; ClarityHealth will treat the two critical gates (hallucination and data control) as immediate-fail conditions per Marissa's definition.
- If the canary passes (weighted score >= 75 and no critical-fail), procurement will sign the MAP and we will schedule a production cutover within two weeks.

Please attach the final MAP and the procurement signoff doc (clarity-signoff-template.docx) and we'll route internally. Our legal team asked for the exact post-canar y report template you mentioned.

Thanks — Bethany
